advances:
The proposed rank-linear information-variance bound is false when, as required by this subgoal, entropy rows on boundary minimal faces are included. The counterfamily consists of complete positive-integer-weight simplices in ambient dimension \(n=3r+1\), has the original full supported integer mean \(\mathbf j=\mathbf1_n\), and satisfies \(\operatorname{Var}_{
u_{\mathbf j}}\log
u_{\mathbf j}\ge r^2\log^2(15/8)/9\). In particular, this also refutes the same bound for \(\log(
u_{\mathbf j}/p)\) when the original source \(p\) is uniform.

proof:
First verify the original support and the large-base encoding; no lattice points are omitted. Write \(S=\sum_{i=1}^rB^{2i-2}\). Since \(S=(T-1)/(B^2-1)\), we have \(L<10rT\). Every displayed weight is positive: the only potentially negative correction occurs in \(w_{x_i}\), and
\(w_{x_i}>T(1-2/B)\ge(99/101)T>0\); all other weights are at least \(T\). Consequently every nonnegative integer point satisfying \(\mathbf w\cdot\mathbf v=L\) has sum of all its coordinates strictly less than \((1010/99)r<11r\).

For such a point define integer digits
\(d_{2i-2}=x_i+z_i+y-3\) and \(d_{2i-1}=-2x_i+u_i+y\), and put
\(K=\sum_{i=1}^r(x_i+3z_i+u_i)+4ry\). Expanding the original equality gives
\[
T(K-9r)+\sum_{k=0}^{2r-1}d_kB^k=0.
\]
The coordinate-sum bound implies \(|d_{2i-2}|<11r\) and \(|d_{2i-1}|<22r\). Therefore
\[
\left|\sum_{k=0}^{2r-1}d_kB^k\right|
<22r\frac{T-1}{B-1}<\frac{11}{50}T<T.
\]
Since \(K-9r\) is an integer, it must be zero, and the digit sum is zero. Reduction modulo \(B\) forces \(d_0=0\), because \(|d_0|<B\). Division by \(B\) and successive reductions force every other digit to be zero. Thus every original support point on the upper equality satisfies precisely the stated equations for \(F_r\).

Conversely, these equations imply \(K=9r\), by summing \(3d_{2i-2}+d_{2i-1}=x_i+3z_i+u_i+4y-9\); they also make the digit sum zero. The same expansion then gives \(\mathbf w\cdot\mathbf v=L\). Hence \(F_r=D_r\cap\{\mathbf w\cdot\mathbf v=L\}\) exactly. Nonnegativity of \(z_i=3-y-x_i\) and \(u_i=2x_i-y\) is equivalent to \(y/2\le x_i\le3-y\). It implies \(0\le y\le2\), and gives precisely the three complete integer layers in the statement.

In the independent real coordinates \((\mathbf x,y)\), the real polytope given by these inequalities is the convex hull of the base cube \([0,3]^r\times\{0\}\) and the apex \((\mathbf1_r,2)\). Indeed, its section at height \(y\in[0,2]\) is the cube \([y/2,3-y]^r\), obtained by mixing the base cube and the apex in proportions \(1-y/2\) and \(y/2\). All base vertices and the apex belong to \(F_r\), and every point of \(F_r\) belongs to this real polytope. Thus it equals \(\operatorname{conv}F_r\), under the stated affine coordinate embedding. The point with \(x_i=1\) and \(y=1\) satisfies all of its defining inequalities strictly, so it is in its relative interior. Its embedded original coordinates are \(x_i=z_i=u_i=y=1\), exactly \(\mathbf j\). Since \(\mathbf w\cdot\mathbf v=L\) is a supporting equality of \(\operatorname{conv}D_r\), and \(\mathbf j\) is in the relative interior of its face \(\operatorname{conv}F_r\), this is the minimal face at \(\mathbf j\). In particular \(\mathbf j\) is an original supported integer point.

Next construct the row and check every original mean. The function
\(g_r(a)=m_0(a)-1+\rho(a)^r a/(1+a)\) is continuous on \((0,1)\). At \(a=1/2\),
\[
g_r(1/2)=-\frac4{15}+\frac13(3/5)^{r/2}
\le-\frac4{15}+\frac13\sqrt{3/5}<0,
\]
where the final inequality follows from \(3/5<16/25\). At \(a=2/3\), \(m_0(a)-1=1/65>0\), so \(g_r(2/3)>0\). A root therefore lies in \((1/2,2/3)\). It is unique: \(m_0(a)\) is strictly increasing, since its derivative with respect to \(\log a\) is the positive variance of the law proportional to \(a^k\), \(k=0,1,2,3\); and \(\rho(a)^2\) is strictly increasing on \((0,1)\), since its derivative is \((1+2a-a^2)/(1+a^2)^2>0\). The other factor \(a/(1+a)\) is positive and strictly increasing as well.

Abbreviate \(a_r,b_r,t_r\) to \(a,b,t\). Summing the original point weights over the three complete face layers gives, respectively,
\[
U(a)^r,\qquad b(a+a^2)^r,\qquad b^2a^r.
\]
Our definition of \(b\) makes the last equal to the first. Moreover
\(b(a+a^2)^r/U(a)^r=[(a+a^2)/\sqrt{aU(a)}]^r=\rho(a)^r=t\), using \(U(a)=(1+a)(1+a^2)\). These are exactly the claimed normalization and layer probabilities
\(p_0=p_2=1/(2+t)\), \(p_1=t/(2+t)\). In particular \(\mathbb EY=1\) exactly.

Conditional on \(Y=0\), the original coordinates \(X_i\) are independent with masses proportional to \(a^k\), \(k=0,1,2,3\), and mean \(m_0(a)\). Conditional on \(Y=1\), they are independent on \(\{1,2\}\), with mean \(m_1(a)=(1+2a)/(1+a)\). At \(Y=2\), every \(X_i=1\). The root equation consequently gives, for every original \(X_i\),
\[
\mathbb EX_i
=\frac{m_0(a)+t m_1(a)+1}{2+t}
=1,
\]
because \(m_1(a)-1=a/(1+a)\). The exact original equations then give \(\mathbb EZ_i=3-\mathbb EY-\mathbb EX_i=1\) and \(\mathbb EU_i=2\mathbb EX_i-\mathbb EY=1\). Thus every coordinate of the original full mean is the integer one; no conditional or projected mean is being substituted for it.

Every law \(\eta\) on \(D_r\) with this full mean is supported on \(F_r\): the nonnegative random deficit \(L-\mathbf w\cdot\mathbf V\) has expectation \(L-\mathbf w\cdot\mathbf j=0\). The constructed \(\nu_{\mathbf j}\) is positive at all points of \(F_r\), and its logarithm there is the affine function \((\log a)\sum_i x_i+(\log b)y-\log\mathcal Z_r\). Thus, for every mean-matched \(\eta\),
\(D(\eta\Vert\nu_{\mathbf j})=H(\nu_{\mathbf j})-H(\eta)\ge0\), with equality only for \(\eta=\nu_{\mathbf j}\). For completeness, nonnegativity and its equality case follow by applying \(-\log q\ge1-q\) at every positive \(\eta\)-mass to \(q=\nu_{\mathbf j}/\eta\): omission of a point of the positive face support makes the summed inequality strict, while with full support equality requires all ratios to be one. This proves the required unique entropy-row identification on the original complete weighted support.

Finally, write \(Q=(\log a)\sum_iX_i+(\log b)Y\) for the original affine score, so \(\operatorname{Var}\log\nu_{\mathbf j}=\operatorname{Var}Q\). Since \(1/2<a<2/3<1\), we have \(0<\rho(a)<1\), hence \(t<1\) and \(p_0=p_2>1/3\). The conditional score means at the two outer layers are
\[
\mu_0=r m_0(a)\log a,\qquad
\mu_2=r\log a+2\log b=r\log U(a).
\]
Their difference satisfies \(\mu_2-\mu_0=r[\log U(a)-m_0(a)\log a]\ge r\log U(a)\ge r\log(15/8)\), because \(\log a<0\), \(m_0(a)>0\), and \(U(a)\ge U(1/2)=15/8\). The law of total variance and the exact finite-distribution variance identity give
\[
\operatorname{Var}Q
\ge\operatorname{Var}(\mathbb E[Q\mid Y])
=\sum_{0\le k<\ell\le2}p_kp_\ell(\mu_k-\mu_\ell)^2
\ge p_0p_2(\mu_0-\mu_2)^2
\ge\frac{r^2}{9}\log^2(15/8).
\]
Since \(n=3r+1\le4r\), division by \(n\) yields the claimed diverging lower bound. Given any proposed finite absolute \(C\), taking an integer \(r>36C/\log^2(15/8)\) violates \(\operatorname{Var}\log\nu_{\mathbf j}\le Cn\). If \(p\) is uniform on the original \(D_r\), then on the sampled face \(\log(\nu_{\mathbf j}/p)=\log\nu_{\mathbf j}+\log|D_r|\), which has exactly the same variance. This is a counterexample to the information-variance claim itself, rather than to a directional fourth-moment claim.
statement:
All logarithms are natural. For each integer \(r\ge1\), put \(n=3r+1\), \(B=100r+1\), and \(T=B^{2r}\). The original coordinates are \((x_1,\ldots,x_r,z_1,\ldots,z_r,u_1,\ldots,u_r,y)\). Define positive integer weights by
\[
\begin{aligned}
w_{x_i}&=T+(1-2B)B^{2i-2},&
w_{z_i}&=3T+B^{2i-2},&
w_{u_i}&=T+B^{2i-1} \qquad(1\le i\le r),\\
w_y&=4rT+\sum_{i=1}^r(B^{2i-2}+B^{2i-1}),&
L&=9rT+3\sum_{i=1}^rB^{2i-2}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Let \(D_r=\{\mathbf v\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^{n}:\mathbf w\cdot\mathbf v\le L\}\), a complete weighted simplex support, and let \(\mathbf j=\mathbf1_n\). Its minimal face support at \(\mathbf j\) is exactly
\[
F_r=\left\{(\mathbf x,\mathbf z,\mathbf u,y)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^{n}:
x_i+z_i+y=3,\quad -2x_i+u_i+y=0\ (1\le i\le r)\right\}.
\]
Equivalently, its complete layers are \(y=0\) with every \(x_i\in\{0,1,2,3\}\), \(y=1\) with every \(x_i\in\{1,2\}\), and \(y=2\) with every \(x_i=1\); in each layer \(z_i=3-y-x_i\) and \(u_i=2x_i-y\).

For \(0<a<1\), put
\[
U(a)=1+a+a^2+a^3,\qquad
\rho(a)=\left(\frac{a(1+a)}{1+a^2}\right)^{1/2},\qquad
m_0(a)=\frac{a+2a^2+3a^3}{U(a)}.
\]
There is a unique \(a_r\in(1/2,2/3)\) satisfying
\(m_0(a_r)-1+\rho(a_r)^r a_r/(1+a_r)=0\). Define \(b_r=[U(a_r)/a_r]^{r/2}\), \(t_r=\rho(a_r)^r\), and \(\mathcal Z_r=U(a_r)^r(2+t_r)\). The law
\[
\nu_{\mathbf j}(\mathbf x,\mathbf z,\mathbf u,y)
=\mathcal Z_r^{-1}a_r^{\sum_{i=1}^rx_i}b_r^y
\quad\text{on }F_r,
\]
and zero on \(D_r\setminus F_r\), is the unique maximum-entropy law on \(D_r\) with original full mean \(\mathbf j\). It is positive at every point of its minimal face and is log-affine there, with original-coordinate score \((\log a_r)\sum_i x_i+(\log b_r)y\). Nevertheless,
\[
\operatorname{Var}_{\nu_{\mathbf j}}\log\nu_{\mathbf j}
\ge\frac{r^2}{9}\log^2(15/8),\qquad
\frac{\operatorname{Var}_{\nu_{\mathbf j}}\log\nu_{\mathbf j}}{n}
\ge\frac{r}{36}\log^2(15/8)\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Thus no finite absolute \(C\) bounds this variance by \(Cn\) throughout the stated row class, including its boundary minimal faces.
